examples.en: In winter I went sledding with the kids.
The sledding hill is really crowded on weekends.

examples.ko: 언덕에서 눈썰매가 너무 빨리 내려가서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The sled went down the hill so fast that I was startled.

examples.ko: 눈썰매 타는 게 생각보다 무섭지 않아요.
examples.en: Riding a sled isn't as scary as I thought.

examples.ko: 동생이 눈썰매를 또 타고 싶다고 졸라요.
examples.en: My little brother keeps begging to ride the sled again.

examples.ko: 이번 겨울에는 눈썰매 말고 스키를 배워 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: This winter I want to try learning to ski instead of sledding.

explain: 보통 '눈썰매를 타다'로 말하고, 놀러 가는 곳은 '눈썰매장'이라고 해요. 스키나 스노보드와 달리 앉아서 타기 때문에 아이들도 많이 즐겨요.
explain_en: People usually say '눈썰매를 타다', and the place to go is called '눈썰매장'. Unlike skiing or snowboarding you ride sitting down, so it is popular with kids too.

en: knowing glance; greeting with a nod

examples.en: I exchanged a nod with a neighbor in the elevator.

examples.ko: 말은 못 하고 눈인사만 짧게 나눴어요.
examples.en: I couldn't speak, so we just briefly nodded at each other.

examples.ko: 선생님이 저를 보고 눈인사로 반겨 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher saw me and welcomed me with a nod.
It was during a meeting, so I just gave a light nod and walked past.

examples.ko: 매일 마주치니까 이제 눈인사 정도는 하는 사이예요.
examples.en: We run into each other every day, so we're at the nodding stage now.
I saw a friend greeting me with a nod from far away.

explain: 말을 하기 어려운 상황이거나 아주 친하지 않은 사이일 때 자주 해요. '눈인사를 하다/나누다/건네다'처럼 쓰고, '눈인사하다' 동사로도 말해요.
explain_en: People use it when speaking is awkward or when they are not very close. It goes with '눈인사를 하다/나누다/건네다', and '눈인사하다' also works as a verb.

examples.en: The departure time was delayed because of the rain.

examples.ko: 회의가 다음 주로 늦춰질 것 같아요.
examples.en: The meeting seems likely to be pushed to next week.
I'm worried because the construction schedule keeps getting delayed.
I don't know why the announcement was suddenly delayed.
I wish the exam date would be pushed back.
I have so much work that lunchtime keeps getting later.

explain: '미뤄지다'와 거의 비슷하게 쓰고, 일정이나 출발 시간이 뒤로 가는 상황에 잘 맞아요. 반대말은 '앞당겨지다'예요.
explain_en: It is used much like '미뤄지다', and fits situations where a schedule or departure time moves later. The opposite is '앞당겨지다'.

en: be trimmed; be polished; be refined

examples.ko: 이 문장은 아직 덜 다듬어져서 어색해요.
examples.en: This sentence isn't polished yet, so it sounds awkward.
The well-kept garden is really pretty.

examples.ko: 여러 번 고쳤더니 글이 많이 다듬어졌어요.
examples.en: After revising it several times, the writing got much more polished.

examples.ko: 머리가 단정하게 다듬어져 있어서 깔끔해 보여요.
examples.en: His hair is neatly trimmed, so he looks tidy.
His rough way of speaking got smoother over time.

examples.ko: 발표 자료가 다듬어지면 다시 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll send the presentation materials again once they're polished.

explain: 머리나 정원이 손질되어 깔끔해질 때뿐 아니라, 글이 고쳐져 매끄러워지거나 거칠던 말투와 성격이 부드러워질 때도 써요. 보통 '글이 다듬어지다', '잘 다듬어진 정원'처럼 쓰고, 다듬는 사람이 있으면 '다듬다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when hair or a garden gets trimmed and neat, when writing gets revised and smooth, and when rough speech or personality becomes gentler. It appears as '글이 다듬어지다' or '잘 다듬어진 정원'. When there is a person doing the trimming, use '다듬다'.

examples.en: I iron my shirts on Sunday evening.

examples.ko: 면 소재는 다림질하기 전에 물을 살짝 뿌려요.
examples.en: I spray cotton lightly with water before ironing it.
I ironed my suit the day before the interview.
I almost burned my hand while ironing.
The shirt I had ironed got wrinkled again right away.

examples.ko: 시간이 없어서 다림질하지 못하고 그냥 입었어요.
examples.en: I had no time to iron it, so I just wore it as it was.

explain: '옷을 다리다', '다리미질하다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요. '옷을 다림질하다'처럼 목적어를 붙여 쓰고, 구김을 펴는 일이라 '구겨지다'와 짝으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People also say '옷을 다리다' or '다리미질하다' with the same meaning. It takes an object like '옷을 다림질하다', and often appears alongside '구겨지다' (to get wrinkled).

examples.en: This café has a lot of regular customers.
The owner gave a free extra to a regular customer.
I'm a regular customer at this hair salon.

examples.ko: 단골손님 덕분에 우리 가게가 계속 문을 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to our regulars, our shop can stay open.
We warmly welcomed a regular who came for the first time in a while.
I went so often that I'm now treated as a regular.

explain: 가게 쪽에서 손님을 부를 때 많이 써요. 손님이 말할 때는 '여기 단골이에요'처럼 '단골'만 써도 되고, 자주 가는 가게는 '단골집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Shops often use it when talking about their customers. A customer can simply say '여기 단골이에요' using '단골' alone, and a place you visit often is a '단골집'.

examples.en: This is my regular place that I go to often.
I have a regular spot near my office.
At my regular place, the owner gives me extra side dishes.

examples.ko: 이사 가서 단골집을 바꿔야 해서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: I moved, so I have to change my regular place, which is a shame.
I went to my usual place with a friend and had soft tofu stew.
The owner of my regular place remembers my name.

explain: 식당, 미용실, 카페처럼 자주 가는 가게에 두루 쓰지만 식당에 가장 많이 써요. '단골 식당', '단골 가게'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It covers restaurants, hair salons and cafés, though it is most common for restaurants. People also say it in parts, like '단골 식당' or '단골 가게'.

examples.en: Today my husband and I watched a movie, just the two of us.
It's the first time the two of us have traveled alone.
Only my sibling and I, just the two of us, were left in the room.
It's an important matter, so I asked to meet one on one.
Being alone together, just the two of us, feels a bit awkward.
There's too much food for just the two of us.

explain: '둘이'보다 다른 사람 없이 오직 두 사람뿐이라는 느낌이 강해요. 주로 '단둘이(서)'처럼 붙여 쓰고, 따로 이야기하거나 데이트할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It stresses that there is nobody else, more than plain '둘이'. It is mostly used as '단둘이(서)', and suits private talks or dates.

examples.en: Pickled radish goes into kimbap.

examples.ko: 자장면을 시키면 단무지하고 양파가 같이 와요.
examples.en: If you order jajangmyeon, pickled radish and onions come with it.
I eat kimbap without the pickled radish.

examples.ko: 단무지 좀 더 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you give me a bit more pickled radish?
Pickled radish is yellow, so it stands out.
Snack bars serve pickled radish as a side dish.

explain: 자장면, 김밥, 분식집에서 빠지지 않는 반찬이에요. 달고 새콤해서 기름진 음식과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a side dish that always shows up with jajangmyeon, kimbap and at snack bars. Its sweet and sour taste goes well with greasy food.

examples.en: When autumn comes, I go leaf-viewing with my family.
Many people go to Seoraksan to see the autumn leaves.
During leaf-viewing season the highways are very congested.
Do you want to go see the autumn leaves this weekend?

examples.ko: 친구들과 단풍놀이를 다녀와서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: I went leaf-viewing with friends and took lots of photos.
The leaf-viewing trip was canceled because of rain.

explain: 보통 '단풍놀이를 가다'로 말해요. 같은 상황에서 '단풍 구경'이라는 말도 자주 써요.
explain_en: People usually say '단풍놀이를 가다'. In the same situation they also often say '단풍 구경'.

examples.en: I walked along the river alone on a moonlit night.

examples.ko: 달밤이 너무 밝아서 불을 켜지 않아도 됐어요.
examples.en: The moonlit night was so bright that I didn't need a light.
That night was a moonlit one with a full moon.
A moonlit night in the countryside is quiet and beautiful.
Caught up in the moonlit mood, I hummed a song.
Taking a walk on a moonlit night calms my mind.

explain: 시나 노래, 이야기에서 분위기를 낼 때 자주 나오는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '달이 밝은 밤'이라고 풀어서 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: It often appears in poems, songs and stories to set a mood. In everyday talk people more often say '달이 밝은 밤' instead.

examples.ko: 매운 닭발을 시켜서 친구와 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ordered spicy chicken feet and shared them with a friend.

examples.ko: 닭발은 처음 먹어 봤는데 생각보다 맛있어요.
examples.en: I tried chicken feet for the first time and they're tastier than I expected.

examples.ko: 저는 닭발이 너무 매워서 물을 많이 마셨어요.
examples.en: The chicken feet were so spicy that I drank a lot of water.

examples.ko: 닭발에는 뼈가 많아서 먹기 조금 불편해요.
examples.en: Chicken feet have lots of small bones, so they're a bit hard to eat.
After work I met a friend at a chicken feet restaurant.
One order of chicken feet to go, please.

explain: 한국에서는 보통 아주 매운 양념으로 볶아서 먹어요. 그래서 '매운 닭발', '닭발집'처럼 자주 말하고, 인기 있는 음식이지만 처음 먹는 사람에게는 낯설 수 있어요.
explain_en: In Korea they are usually stir-fried in a very spicy sauce, so you often hear '매운 닭발' and '닭발집'. It is a popular dish, though it can feel unfamiliar the first time.

examples.en: Write your name on the answer sheet first.
Time was up, so I handed in my answer sheet.

examples.ko: 답안지 칸을 잘못 칠해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I filled in the wrong box on the answer sheet and redid it.
The teacher collected the answer sheets.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 답안지는 뒤에서 앞으로 넘겨요.
examples.en: When the exam ends, we pass the answer sheets from back to front.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터로 채점하는 답안지에는 연필로 써야 해요.
examples.en: On a machine-graded answer sheet you have to write in pencil.

explain: 문제가 적힌 '시험지'와 달리, 답을 쓰거나 표시하는 종이가 '답안지'예요. '답안지를 내다/제출하다/작성하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Unlike the '시험지' (the paper with questions), the '답안지' is the paper where you write or mark answers. It goes with '답안지를 내다/제출하다/작성하다'.

en: being on duty; one's turn; shift

examples.en: Today I'm on cleaning duty.

examples.ko: 청소 당번은 순번을 정해서 돌아가며 맡기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to set an order and take turns on cleaning duty.

examples.ko: 다음 주 급식 당번을 정하는 중이에요.
examples.en: We're deciding who has lunch duty next week.
Whoever is on duty, please erase the board.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 주 당번이 아니라서 먼저 갈게요.
examples.en: I'm not on duty this week, so I'll head out first.
In the duty order, I come right after my friend.

explain: 학교나 직장에서 돌아가며 맡는 일에 써요. '청소 당번', '급식 당번'처럼 앞에 일을 붙이고, '당번을 서다/맡다/바꾸다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for jobs people take in turns at school or work. Put the task in front, as in '청소 당번' or '급식 당번', and say '당번을 서다/맡다/바꾸다'.

examples.en: That person is a great senior of mine from university.
I was very nervous in front of such a senior.
A senior veteran at the company gave me warm advice.

examples.ko: 동아리 대선배들이 후배들에게 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: The old seniors of the club bought the juniors a meal.
To me, he's like a great senior.

examples.ko: 그 분야의 대선배에게 직접 배울 기회가 있었어요.
examples.en: I had the chance to learn directly from a veteran in that field.

explain: '대-'가 붙어서 나보다 훨씬 오래되고 존경할 만한 선배라는 느낌이 나요. 직접 부를 때는 '대선배님'보다 '선배님'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The prefix '대-' adds the feeling of someone far ahead of you and worthy of respect. When addressing the person directly, people more often just say '선배님'.

examples.en: My father had major surgery and is recovering.
I'm relieved the major surgery went well.
After major surgery you have to rest for a while.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 대수술까지는 필요 없다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said I don't need anything as big as major surgery.
I can't sleep with the major operation coming up.
This reorganization is a major overhaul of the company structure.

explain: 병원에서 쓰는 말이지만 제도나 조직을 크게 고칠 때 비유로도 자주 써요. '큰 수술'과 거의 같게 말하고, 반대는 '작은 수술'이에요.
explain_en: It is a hospital word, but it is also often used figuratively for a big overhaul of a system or organization. It is nearly the same as '큰 수술', and the opposite is '작은 수술'.

examples.ko: 자전거 대여료는 한 시간에 삼천 원이에요.
examples.en: The bike rental fee is 3,000 won per hour.
The rental fee was pricier than I thought, so I just bought one.
Insurance is included in the daily rental fee.
Can I pay the rental fee by card too?
Besides the clothing rental fee, you also need a deposit.

examples.ko: 대여료를 조금 깎아 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lower the rental fee a little?

explain: 자전거, 옷, 장비, 자동차처럼 잠깐 빌릴 때 내는 돈이에요. 집이나 건물을 오래 빌리는 값은 보통 '임대료'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the money you pay to borrow things like bikes, clothes, equipment or cars for a short time. The price of renting a house or building long-term is usually called '임대료'.

examples.en: What is the average starting salary for college graduates?
This company only hires college graduates.
Even college graduates find it hard to get a job.
They surveyed the pay gap between college and high school graduates.
The application requirement is a college degree or higher.

examples.ko: 요즘은 대졸자가 너무 많아져서 경쟁이 심해요.
examples.en: These days there are so many college graduates that competition is fierce.

explain: 구인 공고나 뉴스에서 많이 나오고, '고졸자'와 짝으로 자주 써요. 평소 말할 때는 '대학 나온 사람'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It appears often in job postings and news, and pairs with '고졸자' (high school graduate). In casual speech people also say '대학 나온 사람'.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the public bathhouse with my mom.
Every neighborhood has at least one public bathhouse.

examples.ko: 대중목욕탕에서 때를 밀어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever scrubbed your skin at a public bathhouse?

examples.ko: 대중목욕탕에 처음 가면 조금 부끄러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Going to a public bathhouse for the first time can feel a bit embarrassing.
In winter, a lot of people go to the public bathhouse.
This public bathhouse has a sauna too.

explain: 일상에서는 보통 '목욕탕'이라고 줄여 말해요. 찜질방과는 달리 주로 씻고 탕에 몸을 담그는 곳이에요.
explain_en: In daily life people usually shorten it to '목욕탕'. Unlike a '찜질방', it is mainly a place for washing and soaking in the baths.

examples.en: I like popular music more than classical.
We learned the history of popular music in class.
K-pop is also a part of Korean popular music.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 대중음악에 큰 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: That singer had a big influence on popular music.

examples.ko: 대중음악은 시대에 따라 유행이 많이 변해요.
examples.en: Trends in popular music change a lot with the times.

examples.ko: 대중음악과 클래식을 둘 다 즐겨 들어요.
examples.en: I enjoy listening to both popular music and classical.

explain: 클래식 같은 음악과 비교하거나 수업, 기사에서 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서 한국 대중음악은 '가요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when contrasting with classical music, or in classes and articles. In daily talk, Korean popular music is also called '가요'.

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있어서 대추차 한 잔 마셨어요.
examples.en: I felt a cold coming on, so I had a cup of jujube tea.
Jujube tea is sweet and warm, so it's great in winter.
My mom brewed jujube tea at home for me.

examples.ko: 대추차에 잣을 띄워 주는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places float pine nuts in the jujube tea.
At a traditional teahouse I ordered jujube tea and rice cakes.
The jujube tea is still hot, so be careful.

explain: 유자차, 생강차처럼 한국 전통차의 하나예요. 보통 '대추차를 끓이다'라고 하고, 겨울에 몸을 따뜻하게 하려고 많이 마셔요.
explain_en: It is one of the traditional Korean teas, like yuja tea or ginger tea. You usually say '대추차를 끓이다', and people drink it a lot in winter to warm up.

examples.en: The department store is having a big year-end sale.
I bought winter clothes during the big sale.
They say everything is on big discount this weekend.
It was a big sale, so there were really a lot of people.
I heard the big sale only runs until Sunday.
I waited to buy a laptop to coincide with the big sale.

explain: '대-'가 붙어 할인 폭이나 규모가 크다는 느낌을 줘요. 가게 광고에서 많이 보이고 같은 상황에서 '세일'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: The prefix '대-' gives a feeling of a large discount or scale. It shows up a lot in store ads, and in the same situation people also say '세일'.

examples.en: New members are warmly welcome anytime.

examples.ko: 동네 사람들이 새로 온 의사 선생님을 대환영했어요.
examples.en: The neighbors gave the new doctor a big welcome.
Everyone is welcome, so come without worrying.
The atmosphere was so welcoming that I settled in quickly.
Good ideas will always be warmly welcomed.
I was so grateful that the guests welcomed me so warmly.

explain: '환영하다'보다 훨씬 반기는 느낌이 강하고 말투도 친근해요. 모집 글이나 가게 문구에서 '대환영이에요'처럼 명사로도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It sounds much more enthusiastic than '환영하다' and has a friendly tone. In recruitment posts and shop signs you often see the noun form, like '대환영이에요'.

examples.en: It was cold, so I put a cardigan on over my T-shirt.

examples.ko: 날씨가 쌀쌀하면 한 겹 더 덧입어요.
examples.en: When it's chilly, I add one more layer.
If you layer a vest under your coat, it's warm.

examples.ko: 얇은 옷을 덧입고 나가는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to go out with a thin layer added.
I layered a shirt over the dress, and the look changed.

examples.ko: 덧입을 옷을 가방에 하나 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: Put something extra to layer on in your bag.

explain: 이미 입은 옷 위에 한 겹 더 입을 때 써요. 비슷한 '껴입다'가 일상 대화에서 더 많이 쓰이고, 추위 때문에 여러 겹 입는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when you put another layer over clothes you are already wearing. The similar '껴입다' is more common in daily talk and leans toward wearing many layers against the cold.

examples.en: The wall was stained, so I painted over it with white paint.
When the painting dries, I paint another layer on top.

examples.ko: 너무 여러 번 덧칠하면 색이 탁해져요.
examples.en: If you go over it too many times, the color gets muddy.
I want to put another coat of nail polish on.
I painted over the mistake to hide it.
Even without another coat, the color is pretty enough.

explain: 이미 칠한 곳 위에 또 칠할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '다시 칠하다'도 많이 말하고, 나쁜 것을 가리려고 꾸밀 때 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you paint over a spot that is already painted. In daily talk '다시 칠하다' is also common, and it can be used figuratively for covering up something bad.

examples.en: I set a challenging goal and worked hard.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 성격이 도전적이라서 새로운 일을 좋아해요.
examples.en: My friend has an adventurous personality, so he likes new things.

examples.ko: 도전적으로 질문하는 학생이 있어서 수업이 재미있었어요.
examples.en: A student asked questions boldly, so the class was fun.
This assignment is quite challenging.

examples.ko: 저는 도전적이지 않아서 안전한 길을 선택해요.
examples.en: I'm not adventurous, so I choose the safe path.

examples.ko: 도전적일 때도 있지만 대체로 조용한 사람이에요.
examples.en: He can be defiant at times, but he's mostly a quiet person.

explain: 새로운 일에 맞서는 긍정적인 뜻과, 상대에게 맞서는 공격적인 뜻이 둘 다 있어요. 보통 '도전적인', '도전적으로', '도전적이다'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It can be positive, meaning facing new tasks boldly, or negative, meaning confrontational toward someone. It is normally used with endings, such as '도전적인', '도전적으로' and '도전적이다'.

examples.en: It takes about an hour to get to the destination.
Enter the destination in the taxi app first.
The destination is Seoul Station and the departure point is Busan Station.
Contact me when you get off at your destination.
We had lunch somewhere near the destination.
If we're going to the same place, let's take a taxi together.

explain: 교통, 택배, 길 안내에서 많이 써요. 반대말은 '출발지'예요. 비슷한 '목적지'는 가려는 곳이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is common in transport, deliveries and navigation. The opposite is '출발지'. The similar '목적지' leans more toward the place you intend to go.

examples.ko: 아이의 독립심을 키우려고 혼자 자게 했어요.
examples.en: To build my child's independence, I had him sleep alone.

examples.ko: 독립심이 강해서 부모님께 도움을 잘 청하지 않아요.
examples.en: She's very independent and rarely asks her parents for help.
Independence grows little by little from childhood.

examples.ko: 독립심 때문에 아프다는 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: Out of my sense of independence, I didn't even say I was sick.
I want to raise an independent child.

examples.ko: 독립심과 책임감은 같이 자라는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think independence and responsibility grow together.

explain: 나라의 독립이 아니라 스스로 해내려는 개인의 마음을 말해요. '독립심이 강하다/약하다', '독립심을 키우다/기르다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a person's drive to manage by themselves, not a country's independence. It is often used as '독립심이 강하다/약하다' and '독립심을 키우다/기르다'.

examples.ko: 이 책은 청소년 독자층을 겨냥해서 만들었어요.
examples.en: This book was made with teenage readers in mind.
The readership is broad, so anyone can read it easily.
The new novel is popular among readers in their twenties.

examples.ko: 독자층에 따라 글의 말투를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: You have to change the tone of the writing depending on the readership.
The readership is gradually getting older.

examples.ko: 독자층도 달라서 두 책의 분위기가 달라요.
examples.en: The readerships differ too, so the two books feel different.

explain: '독자'는 읽는 사람 하나하나이고, '독자층'은 나이나 취향이 비슷한 읽는 사람들의 무리예요. 책, 잡지, 웹툰을 이야기할 때 '독자층이 넓다/좁다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: '독자' means individual readers, while '독자층' is a group of readers with similar age or taste. It is often used with books, magazines and webtoons, as in '독자층이 넓다/좁다'.

examples.ko: 독해력을 키우려면 매일 조금씩 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To build reading comprehension, you have to read a little every day.
Reading comprehension makes a difference in exam scores.

examples.ko: 독해력이 부족하면 긴 글이 어렵게 느껴져요.
examples.en: If your reading comprehension is weak, long texts feel hard.

examples.ko: 독해력 문제는 시간이 모자라서 다 못 풀었어요.
examples.en: I ran out of time and couldn't finish the reading section.
Compared to my Korean reading, my speaking is weak.
Reading comprehension also definitely improves with practice.

explain: '독해력이 좋다/부족하다', '독해력을 키우다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 요즘은 글을 읽고 이해하는 힘을 '문해력'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It goes with '독해력이 좋다/부족하다' and '독해력을 키우다'. These days people also often say '문해력' for the ability to read and understand text.

examples.ko: 친구 사이에 돈거래는 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to deal in money between friends.

examples.ko: 가족끼리도 돈거래를 하면 사이가 불편해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even among family, lending money can make things uncomfortable.
It was a cash transaction, so there's no record.
I had a money dealing with that person in the past.
I drifted apart from an old friend over a money matter.

examples.ko: 중고 거래로 모르는 사람과 돈거래할 땐 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm careful when dealing with money with strangers in secondhand sales.

explain: 사람 사이에 돈을 빌려주고 받는 일을 말해서 조심해야 한다는 느낌이 자주 있어요. 은행의 공식적인 거래는 보통 '금융 거래'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to lending and receiving money between people, and often carries a sense that you should be careful. Official bank dealings are usually called '금융 거래'.

examples.en: A bundle of cash spilled out of the bag.
There was a scene of counting bundles of cash in the movie.

examples.ko: 돈다발로 값을 치르는 사람은 요즘 드물어요.
examples.en: People who pay with wads of cash are rare these days.

examples.ko: 저 많은 돈다발은 다 어디서 났을까요?
examples.en: Where did all those bundles of cash come from?

examples.ko: 돈다발에 놀라서 한동안 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was so startled by the cash bundle that I couldn't speak for a while.
He took out a card instead of a wad of cash.

explain: 지폐를 묶은 덩어리를 말하고, 영화, 드라마, 뉴스 장면에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '현금'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a bound stack of bills, and often appears in scenes of movies, dramas and news. In everyday talk people just say '현금' (cash).

examples.ko: 절 입구에는 돌계단이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: A long flight of stone steps leads up to the temple entrance.
When I climbed the stone steps, I could see the whole village.
Stone steps are slippery when it rains.
I sat on the stone steps and rested for a moment.
Moss has grown on the old stone steps.

examples.ko: 이 길은 돌계단으로 되어 있어서 걷기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This path is made of stone steps, so it's hard to walk.

explain: 시멘트나 나무 계단과 달리 돌로 만든 계단이에요. 절, 산길, 옛날 집 앞에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: Unlike concrete or wooden stairs, these are made of stone. You often meet them at temples, mountain paths and old houses.

examples.en: There's an old stone bridge at the village entrance.
If you cross the stone bridge, the market is right there.

examples.ko: 이 돌다리는 백 년 넘게 쓰였대요.
examples.en: They say this stone bridge has been used for over a hundred years.
I took a photo on the stone bridge.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에는 돌다리에서 미끄러지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: After rain it's easy to slip on a stone bridge.
The kids played, crossing the stream by the stone bridge.

explain: 돌로 만든 다리예요. 개울에 돌을 띄엄띄엄 놓아 건너는 '징검다리'와는 달리 이어진 다리를 말해요.

phrases.example: 계약서에 사인하기 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요. 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라고 하잖아요.
phrases.en: Check one more time before signing the contract. As they say, test even a stone bridge before crossing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 아는 일이나 튼튼해 보이는 것도 조심해서 확인하라는 속담이에요. 충고할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb telling you to check carefully even things that seem safe or familiar. It is often used when giving advice.

explain_en: It is a bridge made of stone. Unlike a '징검다리' (stepping stones set apart across a stream), it is a connected bridge.

examples.en: A big chunk of rock rolled down from the mountain.
The flour dough became hard as a rock.

examples.ko: 길 한가운데 있던 돌덩어리 때문에 차가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The car stopped because of a rock in the middle of the road.
My bag is heavy as a rock.
I picked the rocks out of the field.
I almost tripped over a rock.

explain: '돌멩이'보다 크고 단단하게 뭉친 느낌이에요. '돌덩어리처럼 딱딱하다/무겁다'처럼 비유로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels bigger and more solid than '돌멩이' (a small stone). It is also often used in comparisons like '돌덩어리처럼 딱딱하다/무겁다'.
